activities.anchor: The pattern in the timeline is worth naming
activities.caption: order the counting milestones chronologically
activities.name: phCountOrder

config.prompt: Between Graunt and Nightingale, the counting instruments were built — order them by year:
items: John Graunt extracts patterns from the Bills of Mortality, inventing vital statistics (1662)
Chadwick's report on the sanitary condition of the labouring population ties filth to fever (1842)
The Public Health Act — the state's first systematic entry into sewerage and water (1848)
Nightingale's polar-area diagrams make statistics an argument ministers cannot ignore (1858)
config.why: Each step is the same move: count, compare, conclude, intervene — evidence precedes action, from 1662's bills of mortality to 1858's diagrams.

activities.anchor: It is a distinct discipline with its own methods
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a discipline briefing
activities.name: phDisciplineSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on what public health is, is wrong — click it:
lines: Public health is a distinct discipline with its own methods.
Its object of study is the population, not the patient.
Its interventions — fluoridated water, seatbelt laws, tobacco taxes, vaccination programmes — operate on everyone at once.
Public health is medicine for poor countries: healthcare without the hospital.
config.correction: Neither 'medicine for poor countries' nor 'healthcare without the hospital' — public health is its own discipline, and its interventions reach the healthy and the wealthy too.
config.why: That misreading hides the field's actual object: whole populations, and the diseases that never happened.

activities.anchor: it is not a hospital system
activities.caption: file each Essential Service under its core function
activities.name: phEssentialSort

config.prompt: The three core functions — file each Essential Service under its half:

items.label: investigate, diagnose and address health hazards and root causes
create, champion and implement policies, plans and laws
build a strong, diverse, skilled public-health workforce and infrastructure

config.why: Assessment counts, policy development decides, assurance delivers — and clinical care for individuals appears only once in the whole list, inside 'assure access'.

activities.anchor: populations die of different things at different stages
activities.caption: call the child-mortality share
activities.name: phChildEst

config.prompt: In 1850s England, roughly what share of children died of infections before their fifth birthday?
config.why: About half — which is why life expectancy 'at birth' of 40 is dragged down mostly by child mortality, not by adults dying young. The epidemiologic transition: infectious killers receded as sanitation, nutrition, vaccines and antibiotics took hold.

activities.anchor: Two measurement tools turn those facts into policy
activities.caption: fill the blanks — counting the burden
activities.name: phDalyCloze

config.text: %%0%% — years of healthy life lost to premature death plus years lived with disability — combine mortality and morbidity, which is why depression and musculoskeletal disorders sit near the top of the global %%1%% tables despite being nearly invisible in death statistics.
config.hint: The first is a three-letter acronym for disability-adjusted life years; the second names the tables they rank.

activities.caption: walk the pyramid — where does the first pound go?
activities.name: phPyramidBranch

config.root: The pyramid's logic is economic as well as moral: the higher up you act, the more people you touch per pound — and the less suffering you have to undo.

start.text: A tobacco-control budget lands on your desk. Where does the first pound go?

choices.label: Preventing uptake — taxes, prices, smoke-free laws
choices.feedback: Averts cases that never need treating, across the whole population.

choices.label: Lung screening for long-term smokers
choices.feedback: Finds tumours while surgery is still curative — for those already exposed.

primary.text: Adult smoking prevalence fell from around 40% in the 1960s to under 15% today — one of the largest single health gains of the century, achieved mostly outside clinics. Now the politics arrives.

choices.label: Push the tax anyway and own the controversy
choices.feedback: Primary prevention regulates the healthy for the sake of the not-yet-sick — which is why seatbelt laws and sugar taxes generate controversies no treatment programme ever does.

secondary.text: Secondary prevention has a real evidence bar: a screening programme is judged by its effect on mortality in controlled evidence, not by how many cases it finds.

done.text: You acted highest in the pyramid: the most people touched per pound, the least suffering to undo.

config.why: Act high in the pyramid wherever the evidence allows — but expect the hardest politics there, because regulating the healthy is never quiet.

activities.caption: true or false — the screening evidence bar
activities.name: phScreenJudge

statements.s: Early detection can add lead time without changing when anyone dies.
statements.why: The clock starts earlier, but the outcome is unchanged — which is why survival-from-diagnosis is not the measure.

statements.s: Some screen-detected conditions would never have caused harm — the overdiagnosis problem.
statements.why: So every screen carries a cost in worry and treatment for conditions that needed nothing.

statements.s: A screening programme is judged by how many cases it finds.
statements.why: By its effect on mortality in controlled evidence — finding cases is not the point.

statements.s: Clearing the evidence bar is the exception, not the default, for screening programmes.
statements.why: Secondary prevention is valuable, but it must earn its place like any intervention.

activities.anchor: Epidemiology's basic designs form an evidence ladder
activities.caption: pair each study design with what it does
activities.name: phLadderMatch

config.prompt: The evidence ladder — pair each design with its move:

pairs.right: follow exposed and unexposed groups forward — the British Doctors Study, 1951
compare the pasts of the sick and the well
allocate exposure by chance, the cleanest test of cause

config.why: Above the ladder sit the Bradford Hill considerations (1965) — strength, dose–response, consistency, plausibility, temporality — refereeing causal claims in the messy observational world public health inhabits.
